teams.heading: Ben Spencer undergoes shoulder surgery to hand Steve Borthwick autumn selection headache
teams.body: Bath scrum-half Ben Spencer is a major doubt for England's upcoming autumn internationals after undergoing surgery on a long-standing shoulder injury. The 34-year-old will miss the opening rounds of the Premiership season, leaving head coach Steve Borthwick with a key selection puzzle ahead of November's opener against Australia. Spencer's club confirmed his post-tour operation, meaning he faces a race against time to be fit. Alex Mitchell and Jack van Poortvliet are the front-runners to fill the void.

teams.heading: France climb to third in Nations Championship after clinical win over Japan
teams.body: France sit third in the Nations Championship table after three matches. Fabien Galthié's side have recorded two wins and one defeat in the tournament so far, following a 42-15 victory over Japan in the most recent round. They have scored 116 points across those opening three fixtures. The defence has conceded 75 points in the same period. When Les Bleus last met Fiji in November 2025, they secured a 34-21 home win. France currently maintain a tournament points difference of +41.

teams.heading: Jack Crowley ruled out for Ireland until the new year
teams.body: Munster have confirmed that fly-half Jack Crowley will not return to action until the new year due to a persistent lower limb vascular injury. The 26-year-old, who has earned 35 caps, has been sidelined since April and will now miss Ireland's November fixtures against Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan stated that "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority" for the playmaker, who was instrumental in Ireland's recent Triple Crown success.

lead.why: This is the most significant personnel update impacting the men's national team availability for the upcoming November block.

teams.heading: Sir Billy Boston passes away aged 92 following distinguished sporting career
teams.body: Welsh rugby is mourning the loss of Sir Billy Boston, who has died at the age of 92. The Cardiff-born icon, one of the most celebrated figures in Welsh sporting history, passed away in his adopted home of Wigan just days after the funeral of his wife, Lady Joan. Knighted last year for his services to the game, Boston remains remembered for his prolific try-scoring prowess and his immense impact on the sport across both codes during a truly legendary career.

lead.why: The passing of a monumental Welsh rugby figure is the day's most significant and widely reported news.

teams.heading: Argentina fall to Australia in tight international contest in Jujuy
teams.body: Argentina suffered a 21-27 defeat to Australia on Saturday in a closely contested international. Despite a spirited second-half effort, the Pumas were unable to overcome the visitors, who secured the win thanks to a decisive try from Tom Hooper and late defensive resilience. Australia coach Les Kiss acknowledged the intensity of the encounter, stating that Argentina’s defence certainly tested his side throughout the match. The result leaves the Pumas looking to refine their execution ahead of future assignments.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One confirms eligibility settlement following high-profile legal challenge
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has revised its controversial player registration rules following a settlement with 24 high-profile players who launched a legal challenge. The dispute centred on proposed category shifts that players argued were discriminatory. Under the updated framework, naturalised players who held citizenship by May 2025 remain in their current registration category. Furthermore, those with 30 or more caps for Japan will now be reclassified from A-2 to A-1, reflecting a significant policy concession by league officials.

lead.why: The settlement of the long-running JRLO legal dispute regarding player registration categories represents a significant administrative shift for the league.

teams.heading: New Zealand fall to Springboks in Cape Town as series tied
teams.body: The All Blacks saw their pursuit of back-to-back victories in South Africa thwarted on Saturday, falling 33-26 to the world champions in Cape Town. Despite crossing the line four times through Roigard, McKenzie, Carter and Savea, the visitors were unable to overcome a dominant first-half display from the hosts. Rassie Erasmus’ side levelled the series at 1-1, setting up a decisive third Test in Johannesburg next Saturday as both teams look to break the deadlock in this rivalry.
